findings.issue_text: [BUG] The Lithuanian totpStep1 translation was replaced with Italian text ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'), not Lithuanian. Lithuanian-locale users on the account console see an Italian instruction sentence where every surrounding string is Lithuanian; the error was introduced by this diff as a copy-paste from the Italian translation.

[BUG] The zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) totpStep1 translation was replaced with Traditional Chinese text ('在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一'), inconsistent with the file's locale. Simplified-Chinese users see a Traditional-Chinese sentence (手機/應用程式 instead of 手机/应用程序) in an otherwise Simplified file — the same file defines mobile=手机 two lines above, so the inconsistency ships in the same screen.

[ADVISORY] The new tests cover only the failure paths (illegal tag, HTML where none allowed, changed anchor); no test exercises the accept path where English contains HTML and the translation's matching HTML/anchors must pass unchanged. A regression in POLICY_SOME_HTML (e.g., allowElements silently dropping 'p'/'b') or in santizeAnchors' accept branch would pass the unit suite; only the repo-wide mojo run over real theme files would catch it, and the normalizeValue workarounds (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, choice-format stripping) have no test at all, so a refactor that breaks them is invisible until a full build fails with a confusing diff message.

[ADVISORY] verifySafeHtml hard-crashes with a bare RuntimeException('unable to read file') when the derived English counterpart path does not exist, instead of a MojoExecutionException or a skip. Any properties file whose English derivation fails — the regex '_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties' on a file without a locale suffix maps 'duplicate_keys.properties' to nonexistent 'duplicate_en.properties', which is exactly why the fixture had to be renamed to duplicateKeys_en.properties in this diff — aborts the whole mojo with a stack trace instead of a diagnosable message, and a RuntimeException escapes the MojoExecutionException contract the rest of verify() honors.

[ADVISORY] normalizeValue resolves '<'-bearing constructs via a hand-maintained per-key allowlist (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*, error-invalid-multivalued-size) even though the matching regexes are already general. The next contributor who adds a message containing a MessageFormat choice pattern or an angle-bracket placeholder gets a build failure with a mangled 'Illegal HTML' diff and must discover this hardcoded key list to fix it; each new such key adds another entry to maintain in verifier code far from the message it unblocks.

[BUG] The Lithuanian totpStep1 message is replaced with Italian text ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'), not Lithuanian. Lithuanian users see an Italian instruction in the Lithuanian login/account UI; the previous correct Lithuanian sentence with the FreeOTP/Google Play links is silently discarded in a PR whose stated intent is adding an HTML sanitizer.

[BUG] The zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) totpStep1 message is replaced with Traditional Chinese text ('在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：' using 手機/應用程式), not Simplified Chinese. Simplified Chinese users get Traditional Chinese characters in the zh_CN locale; the replacement is a wrong-locale string pasted into the zh_CN bundle inside a sanitizer PR.

[BUG] error-invalid-multivalued-size is rewritten from the '{{0}}' escaping scheme to '{0}' plus ICU ChoiceFormat syntax ('{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}') with no change anywhere in the diff to the code that formats this message. This is a runtime rendering-semantics change not traceable to the sanitizer intent: if the consuming formatter (admin console) does not evaluate ChoiceFormat, users see the raw '{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}' fragment in the validation error; the PR ships the message change without the formatter work it depends on.

[BUG] Same untraceable message-format change in account-ui: error-invalid-multivalued-size switches from '{{0}}' escaping to '{0}' + ChoiceFormat with no accompanying formatter update in the diff. Account console renders the multivalued-size validation error through a format scheme the diff never verifies is supported, changing user-visible error output as a side effect of a sanitizer PR.

[ADVISORY] totpStep1 translations in fi, lt, sk, sv and zh_CN are wholesale rewritten to a new shorter sentence ('Install one of the following applications on your phone:'), removing the FreeOTP/Google Play anchor tags and app guidance — content work unrelated to adding an HTML sanitizer. Reviewers of a tooling PR are asked to approve user-facing translation rewrites across five locales; since the old anchor tags already matched the English source, the new checker would not have flagged them, so this drift is not even required to make the verifier pass — and it degrades the message by dropping the app names and download links end users relied on.

[ADVISORY] The new invariant (translations may contain only the HTML the English source has) is enforced exclusively at build time on static in-repo properties files; runtime message overrides are not covered. Realm-level message/localization overrides and custom themes supplied at runtime — the same render-as-HTML channel the sanitizer targets — bypass this check entirely, so the PR's stated security goal ('sanitizer for translated message resources') is only partially achieved; operators may believe translated messages are now XSS-hardened when the override path remains open.

[ADVISORY] normalizeValue hard-codes a growing per-key allowlist (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit, error-invalid-multivalued-size) that couples the verifier's source code to the exact content of individual message keys. Every future English message that legitimately contains a literal '<...>' sequence outside real HTML (another ChoiceFormat argument, another placeholder like <NAME>) breaks the build for all translators and requires a code change to the verifier before the translation PR can land; the list must be hand-maintained in parallel with the message catalogs with no check that the special-cased keys still exist.

[ADVISORY] santizeAnchors pairs translation anchors with English anchors strictly by iteration order (matcher.find()/englishMatcher.find()), not by content, and removes the English anchor via value.replaceFirst(englishMatcher.group()) rather than the occurrence actually matched. A valid translation whose two identical-anchor instances appear in a different order than the English source is rejected with the misleading message 'Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string' even though every anchor matches; when identical anchor strings occur at multiple positions, replaceFirst strips an occurrence other than the one matched, so a translation that mirrors English exactly but with redistributed identical tags can fail or silently diverge from what was checked.

[ADVISORY] English-bundle resolution relies on two blind regex replaceAll calls over the absolute path ('resources-community'→'resources', '_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties'→'_en.properties'), and any resolution failure throws a raw RuntimeException while getEnglishValue silently returns '' for keys missing from English. A locale file whose English counterpart is not located by the string munging (non-standard directory layout, filename not matching the messages_xx pattern, 'resources-community' appearing elsewhere in the path) aborts the whole verification with an unactionable RuntimeException stack instead of the MojoExecutionException the plugin contract uses elsewhere in this class; separately, any key present only in a translation (community translations occasionally add keys) gets englishValue='' and is therefore checked under POLICY_NO_HTML, flagging legitimate HTML in translation-only keys.

[ADVISORY] All three new tests assert only failure paths; there is no test for the allow path — an English message containing HTML whose translation repeats the same allowed HTML, or a translation whose anchors exactly match the English source — so the POLICY_SOME_HTML branch and the passing side of santizeAnchors are never executed by the suite. A regression in the allow path (e.g., a policy or unescapeHtml4 change that starts rewriting allowed

//
markup, or anchor stripping that mangles matching translations) would break the build for every theme translator and only surface as a CI failure on unrelated PRs, because no fixture in this diff pins down what a compliant HTML-bearing translation looks like.

[BUG] The Lithuanian totpStep1 translation was replaced with verbatim Italian text ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'), not a Lithuanian sentence. Every Lithuanian user on the account console OTP setup screen sees Italian text; this is a silent regression of translated content introduced as part of a 'sanitizer' PR, with no human translation review evident.

[BUG] The Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) totpStep1 translation was replaced with Traditional Chinese text ('手機', '安裝', '應用程式'), the zh_TW/zh_HK character set, in a zh_CN file. Simplified Chinese users are shown Traditional Chinese characters for this instruction; the previous zh_CN translation was correct simplified text and was silently overwritten.

[BUG] totpStep1 was rewritten from concrete instructions naming FreeOTP and Google Authenticator (with download links) to a dangling lead-in 'Asenna jokin seuraavista sovelluksista matkapuhelimeesi:' ('Install one of the following applications on your mobile:') with no list following, while the English source key is unchanged in this diff. Finnish users lose the working FreeOTP/Google Play links and read a sentence that references a list that does not exist; the translation now silently diverges from the English source to satisfy the new verifier, with no corresponding English change or human acceptance of the new wording.

[BUG] Slovak totpStep1 was rewritten from instructions naming FreeOTP and Google Authenticator (with links) to a dangling lead-in 'Nainštalujte si do mobilu jednu z nasledujúcich aplikácií:' with no list following, while the English source key is unchanged in this diff. Slovak users lose working download links and see a sentence referencing applications that are never named; translation content changed to pass the new tool without explicit acceptance of the new objective.

[BUG] Swedish totpStep1 was rewritten from instructions naming FreeOTP and Google Authenticator (with links) to a dangling lead-in 'Installera en av följande applikationer på din mobil:' with no list following, while the English source key is unchanged in this diff. Swedish users lose working download links and see a sentence referencing applications that are never named; translation content changed to pass the new tool without explicit acceptance of the new objective.

[BUG] verifySafeHtml() derives the English counterpart path via string replacement and throws a raw RuntimeException when that file does not exist, and verify() now calls it unconditionally — the rename of the test fixture duplicate_keys.properties to duplicateKeys_en.properties in this same diff proves every verified file must now have an _en sibling. Any message properties file verified by theme-verifier whose path does not contain 'resources-community' or whose locale pattern does not match '_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties' (e.g. a locale code outside a-zA-Z, or a file without an English pair) crashes the build with an unhandled RuntimeException and a raw stack trace naming a nonexistent path, instead of the MojoExecutionException diagnostic the tool's contract promises.

[ADVISORY] normalizeValue() hand-maintains a per-key escape hatch (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit, error-invalid-multivalued-size) that must be kept in sync with message content across all themes. Every future translation legitimately containing an angle-bracket placeholder triggers a verifier failure and requires patching this Java allow-list — this very diff demonstrates the pattern twice (templateHelp and error-invalid-multivalued-size both needed special-casing, and zh_CN templateHelp had its '<NAME >' spacing edited to fit the regex); the coupling will repeatedly bite maintainers adding new messages.

[ADVISORY] The RTL exemption is keyed on the substring 'email' appearing anywhere in the absolute file path rather than on the file being an email message bundle, with an acknowledged TODO. Any non-email properties file whose absolute path happens to contain 'email' (e.g. a directory named .../email-notes/ or a login theme under a path containing 'email') silently has ' style="direction: rtl;"' stripped before comparison, masking real content differences from the verifier for those files.

[BUG] verifySafeHtml strips entire MessageFormat choice blocks ({[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*}) out of the value for keys 'error-invalid-multivalued-size' and 'linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*' BEFORE the sanitizer runs, so any HTML placed inside a choice branch is never checked by the OWASP sanitizer yet remains verbatim in the committed translation that ships to users. A malicious or compromised translation contribution can put arbitrary HTML (e.g. or

[ADVISORY] containsHtml() detects HTML with a case-sensitive pattern (<[a-z]+[^>]*>) while the sanitizer and browsers treat tags case-insensitively, so an English source using mixed- or uppercase tags (e.g.
,

, ) is classified as containing no HTML. Every translation of such a key is checked under POLICY_NO_HTML, so translators who legitimately reuse the same
/ markup as the English source get spurious 'Illegal HTML in key ...' build failures and must strip formatting from their locale; the gate fails closed (no exploit), but it produces misleading errors that push contributors toward removing legitimate markup or entity-hacking around the checker.

[ADVISORY] Every new test in this diff asserts that a message IS produced (hasItem(containsString(...))); no test asserts that a translation whose HTML matches the English source produces zero messages, so false-positive regressions in the sanitize/unescape pipeline are uncaught. The pipeline under test contains three fragile fixups (StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4 on both sides, the "<!-- -->" removal, the anchor-stripping in santizeAnchors). If any of them over-corrects, every real theme properties file in the repo starts failing the verifier at build time with 'Illegal HTML' noise, and no unit test in this diff fails — because all four tests only check message presence, never absence. A false positive is the failure mode most likely to burn contributors and it is the uncovered one.

[ADVISORY] All four special-case branches in normalizeValue (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, the {n,choice,...} strip for error-invalid-multivalued-size, and the email RTL style strip) have no test fixture, even though this diff's own change to error-invalid-multivalued-size in messages_en.properties (account-ui and admin-ui) depends on the choice-format branch passing verification. The diff changes two real messages_en.properties files to use '{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}' and simultaneously adds code whose only job is to make that string pass the sanitizer — but the only test coverage is the end-to-end maven build over all theme files. A regression in the regex '\\{[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*}' (e.g. a translated variant with different spacing) surfaces as an opaque 'Illegal HTML in key error-invalid-multivalued-size' build failure across all locales instead of a pinpointed unit failure. Checked test files: misc/theme-verifier/src/test/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessagePropertiesTest.java and the four new fixtures (illegalHtmlTag_en, noHtml_de/en, changedAnchor_de/en, duplicateKeys_en) — none exercises any normalizeValue branch.

[ADVISORY] When an anchor mismatch is detected, santizeAnchors records 'Didn't find anchor tag' and breaks WITHOUT removing the anchor from the value, so the same key then also fails the sanitizer comparison and emits a second, contradictory 'Illegal HTML in key ...' message. One mismatched anchor in a translation produces two differently-worded messages for the same root cause ('Didn't find anchor tag <a ...> in original string' plus 'Illegal HTML in key ...'), and the verifyNoChangedAnchors test (VerifyMessagePropertiesTest.java:48-52) asserts only the first via hasItem, leaving the double-report behavior completely unverified — a refactor that suppresses or changes the second message would silently pass review as intended behavior.

[ADVISORY] The English-counterpart resolution throws a raw RuntimeException (not MojoExecutionException) when the '_en' file cannot be found, and this failure path has no test — evidenced by this diff being forced to rename duplicate_keys.properties to duplicateKeys_en.properties solely so the old fixture name would not crash the new code. Any translation file whose name does not map onto an existing English file under the resources-community→resources rewrite (e.g. a community translation with no English base, or a filename with an unexpected suffix) aborts the maven build with an unhandled RuntimeException outside the plugin's MojoExecutionException error reporting, and the rename in this diff proves the coupling is live; no fixture in VerifyMessagePropertiesTest covers the missing-English case.

[BUG] The Lithuanian totpStep1 message was replaced with Italian text ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'), not Lithuanian. Lithuanian users of the account UI see Italian installation instructions for OTP apps; the new HTML verifier forced removal of the anchor tags and the replacement text was taken from the wrong locale, and nothing in the diff (tests or verifier) checks translation language correctness.

[BUG] The Simplified Chinese totpStep1 message was replaced with Traditional Chinese text ('在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：' — 手機/應用程式 are Traditional forms; the rest of the file uses 认证者/手机 Simplified forms). Simplified Chinese users see Traditional Chinese (Taiwan-style) instructions in the account UI; same root cause as the lt file — the anchor-stripping forced by the new sanitizer check introduced wrong-locale content that no test or verifier check catches.

[BUG] The Lithuanian totpStep1 translation is overwritten with Italian text ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'), silently destroying the existing Lithuanian message with no backup or preservation step. Lithuanian-locale users see an Italian sentence on the OTP setup screen after this build ships; the original Lithuanian string (which also carried the FreeOTP/Google Play anchor links the new sanitizer requires) is lost from the repository and must be re-translated from scratch.

[BUG] The Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) totpStep1 translation is overwritten with Traditional Chinese text ('在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：'), silently replacing the existing Simplified Chinese message. Simplified Chinese users of the account UI are shown Traditional Chinese characters on the OTP setup screen after this build ships; the previous Simplified Chinese translation is overwritten in the same edit that was supposed to only strip disallowed HTML for the verifier.

[BUG] The Lithuanian totpStep1 translation was replaced with Italian text ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'), not Lithuanian. Every Lithuanian-language user setting up OTP in the account console sees Italian installation instructions; the community translation for lt is now wrong-language content shipped to production, and the new HTML verifier cannot catch it because the Italian text is tag-free and passes sanitization.

[BUG] The zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) totpStep1 translation was replaced with Traditional Chinese text (手機/安裝/應用程式), not Simplified (手机/安装/应用程序). Simplified Chinese users of the zh_CN locale are shown Traditional Chinese characters in the OTP setup step; the locale-inconsistent text ships silently because the sanitizer only checks HTML structure, not locale correctness.

[ADVISORY] verifySafeHtml derives the English counterpart path by regex-munging the absolute path and throws a bare RuntimeException ('unable to read file') when that derived path does not exist, instead of a MojoExecutionException diagnostic. Any scanned properties file whose English sibling is not found at the guessed path (no 'resources-community' segment to swap, or no '_en' sibling) aborts the whole build with an unexpected-error stack trace pointing at a fabricated path, rather than a reviewer-actionable message; the regex also silently assumes every locale suffix matches [a-zA-Z-_], so a future file naming pattern produces a wrong English path and the same opaque crash.

[ADVISORY] santizeAnchors breaks out of the loop on the first anchor mismatch, so any additional mismatched or malicious anchors later in the same value are never reported for that key. A translation containing multiple bad anchors produces one diagnostic per build run; the contributor fixes the first anchor, rebuilds, hits the second, and so on — each iteration is a full CI round-trip, and a reviewer auditing the final failure message cannot see how many anchor violations remain in the string.

[ADVISORY] normalizeValue hardcodes a growing per-key exception allowlist (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, error-invalid-multivalued-size, linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*) plus an email-directory path heuristic, making verifier behavior coupled to individual message keys scattered across the codebase. The next message that legitimately contains angle-bracket syntax or an ICU choice fragment fails the build for every locale until someone discovers this class and adds another key-specific branch; the 'email' substring check on the absolute path additionally means any non-email file whose path happens to contain 'email' gets its direction:rtl markers silently stripped from the check.

[ADVISORY] getEnglishValue swallows MissingResourceException and returns an empty string, so a stale community key that no longer exists in English is silently treated as an HTML-free, anchor-free source and then flagged with the misleading message 'Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string'. A contributor whose translation references a removed English key sees an error claiming the anchor is missing from the original string when the actual problem is that the English key itself is gone; the root cause (stale key) is never stated, and the key is silently checked under the NO_HTML policy regardless of what HTML it contains.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new logic in `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()` (OWASP sanitizer policies, `containsHtml()` decision, `santizeAnchors()` matching logic, and `normalizeValue()` special-case workarounds for `templateHelp`, `optimizeLookupHelp`, and choice-format keys). The added unit tests in `VerifyMessagePropertiesTest` cover only negative cases (`illegalHtmlTag_en.properties`, `noHtml_de.properties`, `changedAnchor_de.properties`) plus duplicate keys. There is no test asserting the “accept” behavior when English contains allowed HTML (`br/p/strong/b`) and the translation contains identical allowed HTML/anchors, nor any test covering the `normalizeValue()` exceptions. So a regression in the allowlist policy or the accept-branch of `santizeAnchors()` would not be caught by the unit suite, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] verifySafeHtml hard-crashes with a bare RuntimeException('unable to read file') when the derived English counterpart path does not exist, instead of a MojoExecutionException or a skip. Any properties file whose English derivation fails — the regex '_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties' on a file without a locale suffix maps 'duplicate_keys.properties' to nonexistent 'duplicate_en.properties', which is exactly why the fixture had to be renamed to duplicateKeys_en.properties in this diff — aborts the whole mojo with a stack trace instead of a diagnosable message, and a RuntimeException escapes the MojoExecutionException contract the rest of verify() honors.

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verify(), only IOExceptions from reading the current file are wrapped in MojoExecutionException, but verifySafeHtml() loads both the target bundle and a derived English bundle and on failure throws a bare RuntimeException ("unable to read file"), which will escape verify() unwrapped and can hard-abort the mojo. This is visible in verifySafeHtml(): the English path is derived via absolutePath.replaceAll("resources-community","resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties","_en.properties"), then opened with new FileInputStream(englishFile) and any IOException is rethrown as RuntimeException. If that derived English file does not exist, the plugin will crash with a stack trace instead of producing a MojoExecutionException / diagnosable message.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] normalizeValue resolves '<'-bearing constructs via a hand-maintained per-key allowlist (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*, error-invalid-multivalued-size) even though the matching regexes are already general. The next contributor who adds a message containing a MessageFormat choice pattern or an angle-bracket placeholder gets a build failure with a mangled 'Illegal HTML' diff and must discover this hardcoded key list to fix it; each new such key adds another entry to maintain in verifier code far from the message it unblocks.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces HTML-safety verification in `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()`, and `normalizeValue()` explicitly special-cases only a few keys (e.g., `templateHelp`, `optimizeLookupHelp`, `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*`, `error-invalid-multivalued-size`) to strip/neutralize angle-bracket or MessageFormat `choice` constructs (see the `if/else if` chain in `normalizeValue`). Because the generic choice-pattern replacement (`value.replaceAll("\\{[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*}", "...")`) is gated behind that hardcoded key list, adding a new message key that legitimately contains a `choice` with `<` or other angle-bracket-like content could be flagged as "Illegal HTML" and require updating verifier code. This is a maintainability/architecture concern created by the change, not a currently failing defect shown by the diff.

This is a verifiable localization regression introduced by the PR.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `error-invalid-multivalued-size` in the JS app message bundles from `{{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}}` to `{0}/{1}/{2}` and appends a `{2,choice,...}` fragment (e.g. in `js/apps/admin-ui/.../messages_en.properties` and `js/apps/account-ui/.../messages_en.properties`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new invariant (translations may contain only the HTML the English source has) is enforced exclusively at build time on static in-repo properties files; runtime message overrides are not covered. Realm-level message/localization overrides and custom themes supplied at runtime — the same render-as-HTML channel the sanitizer targets — bypass this check entirely, so the PR's stated security goal ('sanitizer for translated message resources') is only partially achieved; operators may believe translated messages are now XSS-hardened when the override path remains open.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds HTML-safety enforcement only in the build/test tooling (`misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java#verifySafeHtml`), which reads in-repo `.properties` files and reports violations via `messages.add(...)`. There is no corresponding runtime sanitization or enforcement change shown in this PR, so any message content not coming from these checked files would not be covered by this new invariant. The finding’s point about incomplete coverage is therefore a valid scope/architecture concern grounded in what the diff implements (build-time verification only), even though the specific runtime override mechanisms are not shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] normalizeValue hard-codes a growing per-key allowlist (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit, error-invalid-multivalued-size) that couples the verifier's source code to the exact content of individual message keys. Every future English message that legitimately contains a literal '<...>' sequence outside real HTML (another ChoiceFormat argument, another placeholder like <NAME>) breaks the build for all translators and requires a code change to the verifier before the translation PR can land; the list must be hand-maintained in parallel with the message catalogs with no check that the special-cased keys still exist.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `verifySafeHtml()` and `normalizeValue()`, and `normalizeValue()` explicitly special-cases specific message keys (`templateHelp`, `optimizeLookupHelp`, `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*`, `error-invalid-multivalued-size`) to strip/replace patterns involving literal `<...>` or ChoiceFormat fragments before HTML sanitization. This couples the verifier logic to particular catalog keys/content and implies that any future non-HTML `<...>` usage in other keys would require another code change to avoid false "Illegal HTML" failures. The finding’s maintainability/architecture concern is grounded in the new hard-coded per-key allowlist in the diff; it’s not a direct, currently-verifiable functional defect in the PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] santizeAnchors pairs translation anchors with English anchors strictly by iteration order (matcher.find()/englishMatcher.find()), not by content, and removes the English anchor via value.replaceFirst(englishMatcher.group()) rather than the occurrence actually matched. A valid translation whose two identical-anchor instances appear in a different order than the English source is rejected with the misleading message 'Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string' even though every anchor matches; when identical anchor strings occur at multiple positions, replaceFirst strips an occurrence other than the one matched, so a translation that mirrors English exactly but with redistributed identical tags can fail or silently diverge from what was checked.

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors`, anchor tags in `value` and `englishValue` are paired strictly by sequential `matcher.find()` / `englishMatcher.find()` iteration, and any order difference (even with the same set of ``/`` tags) will trigger the error `Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string` because the code does not search for a matching English anchor out of order. Additionally, on a match it removes from `value` using `value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "")`, which removes the first occurrence of that literal anchor string rather than the specific occurrence just matched; with repeated identical anchor tags this can remove a different instance and desynchronize the ongoing `Matcher` scan. This is a real correctness defect in the new verifier logic introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] English-bundle resolution relies on two blind regex replaceAll calls over the absolute path ('resources-community'→'resources', '_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties'→'_en.properties'), and any resolution failure throws a raw RuntimeException while getEnglishValue silently returns '' for keys missing from English. A locale file whose English counterpart is not located by the string munging (non-standard directory layout, filename not matching the messages_xx pattern, 'resources-community' appearing elsewhere in the path) aborts the whole verification with an unactionable RuntimeException stack instead of the MojoExecutionException the plugin contract uses elsewhere in this class; separately, any key present only in a translation (community translations occasionally add keys) gets englishValue='' and is therefore checked under POLICY_NO_HTML, flagging legitimate HTML in translation-only keys.

adjudication.rationale: The new verifySafeHtml() constructs the English bundle path via two regex/string replacements on file.getAbsolutePath() (replaceAll("resources-community","resources") and replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties","_en.properties")), then loads it with FileInputStream. If that derived path is wrong or missing, the code catches IOException and throws a raw RuntimeException ("unable to read file ..."), unlike verify() which uses MojoExecutionException for file errors. This can abort verification with an unhandled RuntimeException based purely on layout/naming. Separately, getEnglishValue() returns "" on MissingResourceException, forcing POLICY_NO_HTML for translation-only keys, which will flag any HTML in those keys regardless of whether HTML is intended.

A regression in the allow path (e.g., a policy or unescapeHtml4 change that starts rewriting allowed

//
markup, or anchor stripping that mangles matching translations) would break the build for every theme translator and only surface as a CI failure on unrelated PRs, because no fixture in this diff pins down what a compliant HTML-bearing translation looks like.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new logic in `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()` with two policy branches (`POLICY_SOME_HTML` vs `POLICY_NO_HTML`) selected by `containsHtml(englishValue)`, and an anchor-allowing path in `santizeAnchors()` when translation anchor tags exactly match the English source. There is no fixture/test demonstrating a compliant case where English contains allowed HTML and the translation retains the same allowed tags, nor a case where matching `<a ...>` tags are accepted without adding a message. So the "allow" paths are not pinned down by the suite in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] normalizeValue() hand-maintains a per-key escape hatch (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit, error-invalid-multivalued-size) that must be kept in sync with message content across all themes. Every future translation legitimately containing an angle-bracket placeholder triggers a verifier failure and requires patching this Java allow-list — this very diff demonstrates the pattern twice (templateHelp and error-invalid-multivalued-size both needed special-casing, and zh_CN templateHelp had its '<NAME >' spacing edited to fit the regex); the coupling will repeatedly bite maintainers adding new messages.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `verifySafeHtml()` and `normalizeValue()` which includes hard-coded per-key special cases (e.g., `templateHelp`, `optimizeLookupHelp`, `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*`, `error-invalid-multivalued-size`) that strip/replace patterns to avoid HTML-sanitizer false positives. The diff also updates message strings (e.g., `templateHelp` and `error-invalid-multivalued-size`) in ways that align with these exceptions, supporting the finding’s maintainability concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The RTL exemption is keyed on the substring 'email' appearing anywhere in the absolute file path rather than on the file being an email message bundle, with an acknowledged TODO. Any non-email properties file whose absolute path happens to contain 'email' (e.g. a directory named .../email-notes/ or a login theme under a path containing 'email') silently has ' style="direction: rtl;"' stripped before comparison, masking real content differences from the verifier for those files.

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.normalizeValue`, the RTL stripping is gated by `if (file.getAbsolutePath().contains("email"))` and then removes the literal ` style="direction: rtl;"` from *any* bundle whose absolute path contains the substring `email`, regardless of whether it is actually an email message bundle. This can hide real content differences from the verifier for non-email properties files located in paths containing `email` (as the finding describes). The comment `// TODO: move the RTL information for emails` further confirms this is a known-scoped hack.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] verifySafeHtml strips entire MessageFormat choice blocks ({[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*}) out of the value for keys 'error-invalid-multivalued-size' and 'linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*' BEFORE the sanitizer runs, so any HTML placed inside a choice branch is never checked by the OWASP sanitizer yet remains verbatim in the committed translation that ships to users. A malicious or compromised translation contribution can put arbitrary HTML (e.g. or

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.normalizeValue(), for keys starting with "linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit" or equal to "error-invalid-multivalued-size", the code does `value = value.replaceAll("\\{[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*}", "...")` before running `policy.sanitize(value)`. This replaces the entire MessageFormat `{...,choice,...}` block (including any content inside its branches) with "...". As a result, if a translation injects HTML inside a choice branch (e.g. `{2,choice,0#|...}`), that HTML is removed prior to sanitization and therefore will not be detected/flagged by verifySafeHtml(), while still existing in the actual shipped `.properties` file. The finding accurately describes this sanitizer-bypass gap created by the normalization step.

adjudication_records.issue_text:
[ADVISORY] containsHtml() detects HTML with a case-sensitive pattern (<[a-z]+[^>]*>) while the sanitizer and browsers treat tags case-insensitively, so an English source using mixed- or uppercase tags (e.g.

/ markup as the English source get spurious 'Illegal HTML in key ...' build failures and must strip formatting from their locale; the gate fails closed (no exploit), but it produces misleading errors that push contributors toward removing legitimate markup or entity-hacking around the checker.

adjudication.rationale:
The diff introduces containsHtml() using `Pattern HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")`, which is case-sensitive and only matches lowercase tag names. In `verifySafeHtml()`, the chosen sanitizer policy depends on `containsHtml(englishValue) ? POLICY_SOME_HTML : POLICY_NO_HTML`. Therefore, if an English source string contains uppercase/mixed-case HTML tags (e.g., `
`, ``), `containsHtml()` will return false and translations will be sanitized with `POLICY_NO_HTML`, causing legitimate markup in translations to be flagged as "Illegal HTML". This is a verifiable correctness defect in the newly added verification logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Every new test in this diff asserts that a message IS produced (hasItem(containsString(...))); no test asserts that a translation whose HTML matches the English source produces zero messages, so false-positive regressions in the sanitize/unescape pipeline are uncaught. The pipeline under test contains three fragile fixups (StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4 on both sides, the "<!-- -->" removal, the anchor-stripping in santizeAnchors). If any of them over-corrects, every real theme properties file in the repo starts failing the verifier at build time with 'Illegal HTML' noise, and no unit test in this diff fails — because all four tests only check message presence, never absence. A false positive is the failure mode most likely to burn contributors and it is the uncovered one.

adjudication.rationale: The added tests in VerifyMessagePropertiesTest (verifyDuplicateKeysDetected, verifyIllegalHtmlTagDetected, verifyNoHtmlAllowed, verifyNoChangedAnchors) all assert that verify() returns at least one message via hasItem(containsString(...)); none assert the absence of messages for a valid/unchanged translation. Given the new, nontrivial sanitization pipeline in VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml() (normalizeValue() unescapeHtml4, santizeAnchors() removal logic, sanitizer output unescapeHtml4, and removal of "<!-- -->"), a regression causing false positives would not be caught by these tests because they never check for an empty result on a “good” fixture.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] All four special-case branches in normalizeValue (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, the {n,choice,...} strip for error-invalid-multivalued-size, and the email RTL style strip) have no test fixture, even though this diff's own change to error-invalid-multivalued-size in messages_en.properties (account-ui and admin-ui) depends on the choice-format branch passing verification. The diff changes two real messages_en.properties files to use '{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}' and simultaneously adds code whose only job is to make that string pass the sanitizer — but the only test coverage is the end-to-end maven build over all theme files. A regression in the regex '\\{[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*}' (e.g. a translated variant with different spacing) surfaces as an opaque 'Illegal HTML in key error-invalid-multivalued-size' build failure across all locales instead of a pinpointed unit failure. Checked test files: misc/theme-verifier/src/test/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessagePropertiesTest.java and the four new fixtures (illegalHtmlTag_en, noHtml_de/en, changedAnchor_de/en, duplicateKeys_en) — none exercises any normalizeValue branch.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial sanitization logic in `VerifyMessageProperties.normalizeValue(...)` with several key-specific branches (e.g., `templateHelp`, `optimizeLookupHelp`, and the `{n,choice,...}` replacement used for `error-invalid-multivalued-size`, plus the email RTL style stripping). The accompanying tests/fixtures added or renamed in this PR (`illegalHtmlTag_en.properties`, `noHtml_en/de.properties`, `changedAnchor_en/de.properties`, `duplicateKeys_en.properties`) do not include any keys/values that would exercise those normalizeValue branches—particularly none includes `error-invalid-multivalued-size` with a `{...,choice,...}` pattern. Since this PR also changes real message strings to include `{2,choice,...|1<values}`, the concern about missing unit coverage for the branch that makes these strings pass the sanitizer is specific and diff-grounded, but it is not itself a demonstrated functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] When an anchor mismatch is detected, santizeAnchors records 'Didn't find anchor tag' and breaks WITHOUT removing the anchor from the value, so the same key then also fails the sanitizer comparison and emits a second, contradictory 'Illegal HTML in key ...' message. One mismatched anchor in a translation produces two differently-worded messages for the same root cause ('Didn't find anchor tag <a ...> in original string' plus 'Illegal HTML in key ...'), and the verifyNoChangedAnchors test (VerifyMessagePropertiesTest.java:48-52) asserts only the first via hasItem, leaving the double-report behavior completely unverified — a refactor that suppresses or changes the second message would silently pass review as intended behavior.

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), value is passed through santizeAnchors() before sanitization. In santizeAnchors(), on a mismatch it adds "Didn't find anchor tag ..." and breaks without removing the offending <a...> tag from value. Since POLICY_SOME_HTML does not allow "a" elements, policy.sanitize(value) will strip the anchor and then the subsequent `if (!Objects.equals(sanitized, value))` will also add an "Illegal HTML in key ..." message for the same entry. The changedAnchor_de.properties fixture would therefore plausibly yield both messages, while the test verifyNoChangedAnchors() only asserts that one message containing "Didn't find anchor tag" exists (Matchers.hasItem), not that the output is singular or free of the second "Illegal HTML" report.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The English-counterpart resolution throws a raw RuntimeException (not MojoExecutionException) when the '_en' file cannot be found, and this failure path has no test — evidenced by this diff being forced to rename duplicate_keys.properties to duplicateKeys_en.properties solely so the old fixture name would not crash the new code. Any translation file whose name does not map onto an existing English file under the resources-community→resources rewrite (e.g. a community translation with no English base, or a filename with an unexpected suffix) aborts the maven build with an unhandled RuntimeException outside the plugin's MojoExecutionException error reporting, and the rename in this diff proves the coupling is live; no fixture in VerifyMessagePropertiesTest covers the missing-English case.

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), the English counterpart is loaded via a derived path (resources-community→resources and locale suffix rewrite) and failures to open it are caught and rethrown as a raw RuntimeException (not MojoExecutionException): `catch (IOException e) { throw new RuntimeException("unable to read file " + englishFile, e); }`. Since verify() does not catch RuntimeException, a missing/mismapped English file will abort the build outside the plugin’s normal MojoExecutionException reporting. The test fixtures were indeed renamed from `duplicate_keys.properties` to `duplicateKeys_en.properties`, consistent with the new `_...\.properties`→`_en.properties` mapping that would otherwise try to open a non-existent `duplicate_en.properties`, and there is no test covering the missing-English-file path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] verifySafeHtml derives the English counterpart path by regex-munging the absolute path and throws a bare RuntimeException ('unable to read file') when that derived path does not exist, instead of a MojoExecutionException diagnostic. Any scanned properties file whose English sibling is not found at the guessed path (no 'resources-community' segment to swap, or no '_en' sibling) aborts the whole build with an unexpected-error stack trace pointing at a fabricated path, rather than a reviewer-actionable message; the regex also silently assumes every locale suffix matches [a-zA-Z-_], so a future file naming pattern produces a wrong English path and the same opaque crash.

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), the English sibling path is derived by munging the current file’s absolute path: `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`, then opened via `new FileInputStream(englishFile)`. If that guessed `_en.properties` path does not exist (or the locale suffix doesn’t match the regex), the code catches `IOException` and throws a bare `RuntimeException("unable to read file ...")`, which is not handled by `verify()` (it only catches `IOException` from `Files.readString`). This will abort the verifier/build with an unexpected stack trace rather than producing a MojoExecutionException diagnostic message.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] santizeAnchors breaks out of the loop on the first anchor mismatch, so any additional mismatched or malicious anchors later in the same value are never reported for that key. A translation containing multiple bad anchors produces one diagnostic per build run; the contributor fixes the first anchor, rebuilds, hits the second, and so on — each iteration is a full CI round-trip, and a reviewer auditing the final failure message cannot see how many anchor violations remain in the string.

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors(), the loop explicitly `break`s on the first mismatch (`else { messages.add(...); break; }`). This means only the first unexpected/mismatched `<a...>` tag in a value triggers the specific "Didn't find anchor tag" diagnostic; subsequent anchor mismatches in the same string are not individually reported by this method. However, the remaining anchors would still be removed by the later OWASP sanitizer (anchors are not in POLICY_SOME_HTML), producing an "Illegal HTML" message, so this is primarily a diagnostics/usability limitation rather than a functional/security defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] normalizeValue hardcodes a growing per-key exception allowlist (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, error-invalid-multivalued-size, linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*) plus an email-directory path heuristic, making verifier behavior coupled to individual message keys scattered across the codebase. The next message that legitimately contains angle-bracket syntax or an ICU choice fragment fails the build for every locale until someone discovers this class and adds another key-specific branch; the 'email' substring check on the absolute path additionally means any non-email file whose path happens to contain 'email' gets its direction:rtl markers silently stripped from the check.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `verifySafeHtml()` and `normalizeValue()`, where `normalizeValue` contains explicit per-key branches (`templateHelp`, `optimizeLookupHelp`, `error-invalid-multivalued-size`, and `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*`) and a path-based heuristic `if (file.getAbsolutePath().contains("email"))` to strip `style="direction: rtl;"`. This is indeed coupling verifier behavior to specific message keys and to file path substrings, making it fragile/maintenance-heavy as new legitimate angle-bracket/choice syntax appears in other keys/locales. The claim about future builds failing is a plausible architectural risk grounded in this code, not a directly provable runtime defect today.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getEnglishValue swallows MissingResourceException and returns an empty string, so a stale community key that no longer exists in English is silently treated as an HTML-free, anchor-free source and then flagged with the misleading message 'Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string'. A contributor whose translation references a removed English key sees an error claiming the anchor is missing from the original string when the actual problem is that the English key itself is gone; the root cause (stale key) is never stated, and the key is silently checked under the NO_HTML policy regardless of what HTML it contains.

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.getEnglishValue(), a MissingResourceException is caught and "" is returned. verifySafeHtml() then uses this empty englishValue as the source-of-truth for both anchor validation (santizeAnchors compares against englishValue) and HTML policy selection (containsHtml(englishValue) -> POLICY_NO_HTML). If a community translation contains a key missing from the English bundle, any <a> tag will trigger "Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string" and any HTML will be judged under NO_HTML, producing misleading errors without ever reporting the real issue (stale/missing English key). This behavior is directly verifiable from the added code paths in the diff.
